_comment: Adversarial-review dispositions for the TACTICAL domain, read by tools/migration_loop.py's review_gate(). A function the manifest flags review_required (writes a roster region OR size>p90 OR is root) may not be promoted to `verified` without an entry here. Shape: "<function name>": {"disposition": "reviewed"|"exempt", "session": "<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>", "by": "<reimpl-verify workflow / agent>", "note": "<evidence, or why no shadow/review applies>"}. A `reviewed` entry MUST name the `session` that ran the review: the driver cross-checks that that session's captured agents (session_reports/loop/<session>/agents.json) actually include an adversarial-review spawn -- a bare `reviewed` with no spawn is rejected. An `exempt` entry needs no agent (it is an explicit human-auditable decision). `reviewed` = run through .claude/workflows/reimpl-verify.js; `exempt` = the session judged the body un-shadowable / exhaustively oracle-covered and SAID SO. Keys beginning with _ are comments. Rows already verified when the gate landed (2026-08-26) carry explicit grandfather exempt entries (backfilled same day). Two layers now read this file: migration_loop.py gates the TRANSITION to verified per session and cross-checks agent backing; migration_session.py --end fails while ANY review_required+verified row lacks a disposition, so a skip is caught in-session.

(1) door_clear_leaf_tile's k-sub-loop bound was hardcoded to 6 for BOTH leaves; the original uses 6 for the right leaf (0x004325a5, CMP [EBP-0x34],0x6) but 8 for the left leaf (0x00432827, CMP [EBP-0x34],0x8) -- independently re-confirmed against tmp/decomp_tact/llm_tact_door_update_tile_state_004324c0.asm before applying. Added regression case T23 (tact_door_selftest.cpp) asserting height_row[6]/[7] survive the right leaf's clear but not the left leaf's. Mutation-tested by reverting the left-leaf bound to 6: T23 failed exactly as predicted (2 checks), reverted, confirmed green (4542 checks, 0 failures). Full DLL rebuild PASS after the fix.

llm_tact_unit_teleport.by: .claude/workflows/reimpl-verify.js (batch mode, 3 lens-group reviewers + 1 adjudicator, run wf_e81b9d54-1b6)
llm_tact_unit_teleport.note: verdict: DIVERGES on the first pass -- a REAL bug found and fixed before promotion, not a false positive. One lens reviewer (semantics group) and the adjudicator INDEPENDENTLY re-derived the same divergence from the raw bytes: the DIRECT-path RANDOM (mode==1) post-loop slot-validity check used `!(dest_col_at(tz,slot)!=0 && dest_row_at(tz,slot)!=0)` (De Morgan-equivalent to 'reset if EITHER field is zero'), but the original (@0x00432fc1-0x00432fe9, JNZ/JZ shape) resets the slot only when BOTH dest_col AND dest_row are zero -- identical shape to the SEQUENCE-mode reset the draft got right one branch earlier. A slot with column==0 and a nonzero row (a legitimate map-edge coordinate) was wrongly treated as empty and reset to slot 0, landing the unit on the wrong tile. Independently re-derived and confirmed by the conductor before applying (not applied on the reviewer's claim alone): fixed to `dest_col_at(tz, slot) == 0 && dest_row_at(tz, slot) == 0`, added regression case T12b (tact_unit_teleport_selftest.cpp) using the reviewer's own concrete input (slots 0-2 populated, slot 3 = (0,20), rand()/4096==3), mutation-tested by reverting to the buggy form -- T12b failed exactly as predicted, reverted clean. Full DLL rebuild + `test_ui.py --tact-determinism --tact-synth --tact-selftest` re-run PASS after the fix. Second lens reviewer (representation group) and the adjudicator both also independently confirmed the draft's reuse of early-captured cur_col/cur_row locals (instead of re-reading unit.pos_col/pos_row at the old-position clear sites) is equivalence-preserving -- llm_tact_unit_vision_remove reads but never writes those fields, confirmed by reading its own .asm. Third lens reviewer (environment group) found no issues. No rig arm exists for this function (arm_ready:false, TACT-CUT2) -- the offline oracle is the only proof this correction has, so the review is load-bearing rather than a secondary check.

llm_strat_squad_assault_resolve.by: .claude/workflows/reimpl-verify.js (batch mode, 3 lens-group reviewers + 1 adjudicator, run wf_a2e2e625-e92)
llm_strat_squad_assault_resolve.note: verdict: DIVERGES on the FIRST PASS, not a false alarm -- all three reviewers independently caught the same bug: the draft collapsed the original's genuine 3-way branch (loss<=0 -> kill; loss>0 && delta(=energy-loss)>0 -> pending_damage; loss>0 && delta<=0 -> TRUE NO-OP, the original's JNC @0x0044d959 jumps straight past both the kill block and the pending_damage add) into a 2-way if/else, routing the no-op case into the kill arm. Independently re-derived from the raw bytes before applying (FLDZ/FCOMP/FNSTSW/SAHF/JC @0x0044d8f8-0x0044d900 and the second FLDZ/FCOMP/JNC @0x0044d951-0x0044d959) -- confirmed the reviewers' reading. Fixed to the 3-way branch, added regression case T2 (loss>0 && delta<=0 must NOT call remove_from_map/teardown and must NOT touch pending_damage/units_lost_total), mutation-tested by reverting to the 2-way collapse (T2 failed exactly as predicted, 3 checks), reverted, confirmed green (1039 checks, 0 failures). Full DLL rebuild + run_selftests.py (ASan+plain) + lint_repo.py + test_ui.py --tact-determinism --tact-synth --tact-selftest all PASS after the fix. One reviewer-raised note (scan_player's uint16_t truncation in the teardown call vs the draft's plain uint32_t cast) was independently confirmed a non-issue: scan_player is a tiny player index, never near 0x10000, so the two representations are observably identical for every value the field can hold -- no action taken. VERIFIED/T2 (offline oracle only -- no rig arm exists or ever will for this function, since its own two direct calls are TACT-CUT2-ungated effectful shared callees).

llm_tact_unit_destroy.by: .claude/workflows/reimpl-verify.js (batch mode, 3 lens-group reviewers + 1 adjudicator, run wf_c3236abe-45f)
llm_tact_unit_destroy.note: verdict: DIVERGES on the first pass -- a REAL bug found and fixed before promotion, not a false positive. All 3 lens-group reviewers AND the adjudicator independently re-derived the same divergence from the raw bytes: the footprint-clear sweep's block at 0x00431e8b-0x00431ebc reads `col` with NO increment (contrast the genuine +1-col candidates at 0x00431e58/0x00431ebf, which DO `INC EAX` before the shift) and adds a fixed +8 to the tile_object base -- since row-stride is 8 bytes (row<<3) and col-stride is 0x800 (col<<0xb), that block is (col, row+1), not (col+1, row+1) as the draft/header/oracle all transcribed it. The immediately-following block at 0x00431ebc-0x00431eef IS the true (col+1, row+1) check (INC EAX present). The draft collapsed both into a single `clear_if_match(col + 1, row + 1)` call, silently dropping the (col, row+1) candidate from the 9-tile search entirely -- a unit destroyed while stamped at (col, row+1) would leave that tile's `tile_objects[].building` dangling, read by later spawn-placement/pathing/vision passes as if the destroyed unit still occupied it. Independently re-derived from tmp/decomp_tact/llm_tact_unit_destroy_00431d8d.asm before applying (not applied on the reviewers' claim alone): confirmed the exact instruction sequence at 0x00431e8b-0x00431eef. Fixed tact_unit_destroy.cpp to two separate calls (col, row+1) then (col+1, row+1); corrected tact_unit_destroy.h's candidate list (was missing a row, said 'up to 8' instead of 9); corrected the T2 selftest, which had planted its decoy at the WRONG tile ((col+1,row+1) instead of (col,row+1)) and so could not have caught this. Mutation-tested by reverting to the buggy single-call form: T2 failed exactly as predicted (`got 0x0000000c, want 0x00000000` at the (col,row+1) tile), reverted, confirmed green (4477 checks, 0 failures). Full rebuild + run_selftests.py (ASan+plain) PASS after the fix. VERIFIED/T2 (offline oracle only -- no rig arm exists per the manifest's measured 29-function/55-region closure).

llm_tact_frame.note: verdict: DIVERGES on the first pass -- a REAL bug found and fixed before promotion, not a false positive. The sentinel-lens reviewer and the adjudicator independently caught it: the draft computed shift_held = (RSHIFT|LSHIFT) ONCE before step 10 and reused that single snapshot at 5 later, independent gate sites (draft lines 301/312/336/350/381, steps 18/19/20b/21/23a), while the original re-reads the live RSHIFT/LSHIFT globals fresh at each of 7 sites (0x00429f24, 0x0042a01e, 0x0042a437, 0x0042a4d9, 0x0042a696, 0x0042a74b, 0x0042a910), each into its own distinct stack slot, never a cached local. Between the first 2 sites (steps 10/12, contiguous, no intervening calls -- caching there is provably safe) and the other 5, the original calls mouse_delta_pump/mouse_buttons_get/gfx_LoadSprite x2/render_view/door_tick/teleport_zone_scan_tick/sidebar_dispatch/up to 4 view_shift_*/cam_follow_selection_tick -- any of which could interleave with a real Shift-key transition. Independently re-confirmed against tmp/decomp_tact/llm_tact_frame_00429b1a.asm before applying (all 7 TEST-byte-ptr sites and their distinct stack slots). Fixed: kept the cached shift_held local only for the two contiguous step-10/12 uses, added a shift_now() lambda re-reading *v.key_rshift_held/*v.key_lshift_held live, and routed the 5 later sites (lines 301,312,336,350,381 pre-fix) through it. Rebuilt; run_selftests.py + lint_repo.py + tact-determinism gate re-run after the fix (see this session's report for the exact commands/results). The other two adjudicated findings (severity=note) were REJECTED as new issues -- both merely restate uncertainties tact_frame.h already flags explicitly (step-3 empty-queue stack-read modeling choice; step-13 mouse_buttons_cur width) and add no new resolution; left as-is per the header's existing UNCERTAINTY framing. This function cannot be shadow-armed offline (tacttest cannot drive mouse/keyboard); its only proof instrument is test_ui.py --tact-determinism, so this review was the PRIMARY correctness evidence, not a secondary check.

llm_tact_ui_sel_panel_multi_mode_tick.note: verdict: equivalent, no fix-required findings (ready_to_arm). All three reviewers + the adjudicator independently examined the header's own documented block-5c asymmetry (camera-recenter: column center subtracts win_w/0x40 but the column CLAMP subtracts win_w/0x20; row center subtracts view_tiles_h/2 but the row CLAMP subtracts the FULL view_tiles_h) and confirmed it is a genuine, correctly-preserved asymmetry in the original -- hand-simulated the SAR/SHL/SBB and SAR/SUB/SAR bit sequences at 0x00436835-0x0043691a for representative negative inputs and matched plain C++ truncating division bit-for-bit; cross-checked against *v.map_width/*v.map_height (_G_LLM_TACT_MAP_WIDTH_CACHE/_HEIGHT_CACHE) and the clamp comparison direction. No fix applied -- explicitly NOT a bug. Every outward call this body makes is a mocked frontier callee in its own _calls struct (including llm_tact_unit_enqueue_command), so unlike some TACT1E siblings this function reaches no unmapped real game VA and is fully offline-oracle-testable; oracle authored this same session (tact_ui_sel_panel_multi_mode_tick_selftest.cpp).
